requirements.original: TTCN-3 permits the specification of length restrictions on string types.
requirements.canonical: A length restriction MAY be specified on a string type.

examples.text:
type bitstring MyByte length(8);  // Exactly length 8 
  type bitstring MyByte length(8 .. 8);  // Exactly length 8 
  type bitstring MyNibbleToByte length(4 .. 8); // Minimum length 4, maximum length 8

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.4 -- TTCN-3 permits the specification of length restrictions on string types.

requirements.original: The length boundaries are based on different units depending on the string type with which they are used.
requirements.canonical: The unit of the length boundaries of a length restriction depends on the string type with which it is used, as specified in table 4.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.4 -- The length boundaries are based on different units depending on the string type with which they are used.

requirements.original: In all cases, these boundaries shall be inclusive boundaries only and evaluate to non-negative integer values (or derived integer values).
requirements.canonical: A length boundary of a string length restriction SHALL be an inclusive boundary only.

examples.text:
type bitstring MyByte length(8);  // Exactly length 8 
  type bitstring MyByte length(8 .. 8);  // Exactly length 8 
  type bitstring MyNibbleToByte length(4 .. 8); // Minimum length 4, maximum length 8

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.4 -- In all cases, these boundaries shall be inclusive boundaries only and evaluate to non-negative integer values (or derived integer values).

requirements.original: In all cases, these boundaries shall be inclusive boundaries only and evaluate to non-negative integer values (or derived integer values).
requirements.canonical: A length boundary of a string length restriction SHALL evaluate to a non-negative `integer` value (or a value of a type derived from `integer`).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.4 -- In all cases, these boundaries shall be inclusive boundaries only and evaluate to non-negative integer values (or derived integer values).

requirements.original: For the upper bound the keyword infinity should also be used to indicate that there is no upper limit for the length.
requirements.canonical: The keyword `infinity` MAY be used as the upper boundary of a length restriction to indicate that there is no upper limit for the length.

ambiguity.issue: 'should also be used' most likely expresses a permission (infinity can be used); read literally it is a recommendation. The permission reading was chosen.
readings: The keyword `infinity` MAY be used as the upper boundary of a length restriction to indicate that there is no upper limit for the length.
The keyword `infinity` SHOULD be used as the upper boundary of a length restriction when there is no upper limit for the length.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.4 -- For the upper bound the keyword infinity should also be used to indicate that there is no upper limit for the length.

requirements.original: The upper boundary shall be greater than or equal to the lower boundary.
requirements.canonical: The upper boundary of a length restriction SHALL be greater than or equal to the lower boundary.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.4 -- The upper boundary shall be greater than or equal to the lower boundary.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows using character patterns specified in clause B.1.5 to constrain permitted values of charstring and universal charstring types.
requirements.canonical: A character pattern as specified in clause B.1.5 MAY be used to constrain the permitted values of `charstring` and `universal charstring` types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.5 -- TTCN-3 allows using character patterns specified in clause B.1.5 to constrain permitted values of charstring and universal charstring types.

requirements.original: The type constraint shall use the pattern keyword followed by a character pattern.
requirements.canonical: A pattern subtype constraint SHALL consist of the keyword `pattern` followed by a character pattern.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.5 -- The type constraint shall use the pattern keyword followed by a character pattern.

requirements.original: All values denoted by the pattern shall be a subset of the type being sub typed.
requirements.canonical: All values denoted by the character pattern of a pattern subtype constraint SHALL be a subset of the values of the type being subtyped.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.5 -- All values denoted by the pattern shall be a subset of the type being sub typed.

requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions defining the values shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.
requirements.canonical: A constant used in a constant expression defining a pattern subtype constraint SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.5 -- Constants used in the constant expressions defining the values shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.

requirements.original: Within integer and float (or derivations of these types) subtype definitions it is allowed to mix lists and ranges.
requirements.canonical: An `integer` or `float` subtype definition (or a subtype definition of a type derived from them) MAY mix list and range constraints.

examples.text:
type integer MyIntegerRange (1, 2, 3, 10 .. !20, 99, 100);
  type float LessThanPiAndNaN (-infinity .. 3142E-3, not_a_number);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.1 -- Within integer and float (or derivations of these types) subtype definitions it is allowed to mix lists and ranges.

requirements.original: It is possible to mix both template list and type list subtyping with each other and with range subtyping.
requirements.canonical: A subtype definition MAY mix template list and type list constraints with each other and with range constraints.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence does not state the types it applies to; since mixing is forbidden for character string types (6.1.2.6.1-s011), it was read as applying to integer and float subtype definitions.
readings: Within integer and float subtype definitions, template list and type list constraints MAY be mixed with each other and with range constraints.
Within any subtype definition, template list and type list constraints MAY be mixed with each other and with range constraints.

examples.text:
type integer MyIntegerRange (1, 2, 3, 10 .. !20, 99, 100);
  type float LessThanPiAndNaN (-infinity .. 3142E-3, not_a_number);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.1 -- It is possible to mix both template list and type list subtyping with each other and with range subtyping.

requirements.original: Overlapping of different constraints is not an error.
requirements.canonical: Overlapping of different constraints in a subtype definition is not an error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.1 -- Overlapping of different constraints is not an error.

requirements.original: Type: bitstring; Units of Length: bits
requirements.canonical: The unit of length of a length restriction on `bitstring` is bits.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.1 -- Type: bitstring; Units of Length: bits

requirements.original: Type: hexstring; Units of Length: hexadecimal digits
requirements.canonical: The unit of length of a length restriction on `hexstring` is hexadecimal digits.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.1 -- Type: hexstring; Units of Length: hexadecimal digits

requirements.original: Type: octetstring; Units of Length: octets
requirements.canonical: The unit of length of a length restriction on `octetstring` is octets.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.1 -- Type: octetstring; Units of Length: octets

requirements.original: Type: character strings; Units of Length: characters
requirements.canonical: The unit of length of a length restriction on a character string type (`charstring`, `universal charstring`) is characters.

ambiguity.issue: 'character strings' is not a type name; the character string types charstring and universal charstring are meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.1 -- Type: character strings; Units of Length: characters

requirements.original: Within charstring and universal charstring subtype definitions it is not allowed to mix pattern, template list, type list, or range constraints.
requirements.canonical: A `charstring` or `universal charstring` subtype definition SHALL NOT mix pattern, template list, type list or range constraints.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.1 -- Within charstring and universal charstring subtype definitions it is not allowed to mix pattern, template list, type list, or range constraints.

requirements.original: Within bitstring, hexstring, `octetstring subtype definitions lists and length restriction may be mixed in` the same subtype definition.
requirements.canonical: A `bitstring`, `hexstring` or `octetstring` subtype definition MAY mix list constraints and a length restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.2 -- Within bitstring, hexstring, `octetstring subtype definitions lists and length restriction may be mixed in` the same subtype definition.

requirements.original: Within charstring and universal charstring subtype definitions it is allowed to add a length restriction to constraints containing list, range or pattern subtyping in the same subtype definition.
requirements.canonical: A `charstring` or `universal charstring` subtype definition MAY add a length restriction to a list, range or pattern constraint.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.2 -- Within charstring and universal charstring subtype definitions it is allowed to add a length restriction to constraints containing list, range or pattern subtyping in the same subtype definition.

requirements.original: When mixed with other constraints the length restriction shall be the last element of the subtype definition.
requirements.canonical: When mixed with other constraints, the length restriction SHALL be the last element of the subtype definition.
requirements.condition: the length restriction is mixed with other constraints
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.2 -- When mixed with other constraints the length restriction shall be the last element of the subtype definition.

requirements.original: The length restriction takes effect jointly with other subtyping mechanisms (i.e. the value set of the type consists of the common subset of the value sets identified by the list, range or pattern subtyping and the length restriction).
requirements.canonical: A length restriction mixed with list, range or pattern constraints yields a value set that is the intersection of the value sets of those constraints and of the length restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.2.6.2 -- The length restriction takes effect jointly with other subtyping mechanisms (i.e. the value set of the type consists of the common subset of the value sets identified by the list, range or pattern subtyping and the length restriction).

requirements.original: The type keyword is also used to specify structured types such as record types, record `of types, set types, set` of types, enumerated types, union types and map types.
requirements.canonical: The keyword `type` is used to specify structured types: record types, record of types, set types, set of types, enumerated types, union types and map types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- The type keyword is also used to specify structured types such as record types, record `of types, set types, set` of types, enumerated types, union types and map types.

requirements.original: Values of these types may be given using an explicit assignment notation or a short-hand value list notation or in a mixed list and assignment notation.
requirements.canonical: A value of a structured type MAY be given using assignment notation, value list notation or mixed list and assignment notation, as applicable to the type.

ambiguity.issue: 'these types' includes enumerated, union and map types, for which not all notations apply (see 6.2.0-s005/s008); the reading restricted to applicable types was chosen.
readings: A value of a structured type MAY be given using assignment notation, value list notation or mixed notation, as applicable to the type.
A value of any of the listed structured types (including enumerated, union and map types) MAY be given using any of assignment, value list or mixed notation.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- Values of these types may be given using an explicit assignment notation or a short-hand value list notation or in a mixed list and assignment notation.

requirements.original: The assignment and the mixed notation can be used for record, record of, set, set `of and map value` notations and for arrays.
requirements.canonical: Assignment notation and mixed notation MAY be used for record, record of, set, set of and map values and for arrays.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- The assignment and the mixed notation can be used for record, record of, set, set `of and map value` notations and for arrays.

requirements.original: In these notations each assigned field or index shall not appear more than once and assignments to fields or indexes given in list notation are not allowed.
requirements.canonical: In assignment notation or mixed notation, an assigned field or index SHALL NOT appear more than once.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- In these notations each assigned field or index shall not appear more than once and assignments to fields or indexes given in list notation are not allowed.

requirements.original: In these notations each assigned field or index shall not appear more than once and assignments to fields or indexes given in list notation are not allowed.
requirements.canonical: In mixed notation, a field or index already given in the value list part SHALL NOT be assigned again in the assignment part.

ambiguity.issue: 'assignments to fields or indexes given in list notation' can mean re-assigning elements already set by the list part, or using assignment syntax within the list part; the first reading was chosen.
readings: In mixed notation, a field or index already given in the value list part SHALL NOT be assigned again in the assignment part.
Within value list notation, assignments to fields or indexes SHALL NOT be used.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- In these notations each assigned field or index shall not appear more than once and assignments to fields or indexes given in list notation are not allowed.

requirements.original: The assignment notation can also be used for union values.
requirements.canonical: Assignment notation MAY be used for union values.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- The assignment notation can also be used for union values.

requirements.original: The value list notation can be used for record, record of, set and set `of value notations and` for arrays.
requirements.canonical: Value list notation MAY be used for record, record of, set and set of values and for arrays.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- The value list notation can be used for record, record of, set and set `of value notations and` for arrays.

requirements.original: The index notation as part of an assignment or mixed notation can be used as the left-hand side of element assignments for record of, set `of and map value notations and for arrays.
requirements.canonical: Index notation MAY be used as the left-hand side of element assignments in assignment notation or mixed notation for record of, set of and map values and for arrays.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- The index notation as part of an assignment or mixed notation can be used as the left-hand side of element assignments for record of, set `of and map value notations and for arrays.

requirements.original: In this notation each index shall not` appear more than once and shall conform to the range of indices allowed by the type definition.
requirements.canonical: In index notation within an assignment or mixed notation, an index SHALL NOT appear more than once.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- In this notation each index shall not` appear more than once and shall conform to the range of indices allowed by the type definition.

requirements.original: In this notation each index shall not` appear more than once and shall conform to the range of indices allowed by the type definition.
requirements.canonical: In index notation within an assignment or mixed notation, each index SHALL conform to the range of indices allowed by the type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- In this notation each index shall not` appear more than once and shall conform to the range of indices allowed by the type definition.

requirements.original: It is allowed to mix the two value notations in the same (immediate) context only in such a way that elements in list notation do not follow elements in assignment notation.
requirements.canonical: In mixed notation, an element in value list notation SHALL NOT follow an element in assignment notation within the same immediate context.

examples.text:
// This is disallowed
  const MyRecordType c_myRecordValue:= {c_myIntegerValue, field2 := true, "A string"}

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- It is allowed to mix the two value notations in the same (immediate) context only in such a way that elements in list notation do not follow elements in assignment notation.

requirements.original: Where applicable TTCN-3 type definitions may be recursive.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 type definition MAY be recursive where applicable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- Where applicable TTCN-3 type definitions may be recursive.

requirements.original: The user, however, shall ensure that all type recursion is resolvable and that no infinite recursion occurs.
requirements.canonical: A recursive type definition SHALL be resolvable.

ambiguity.issue: 'The user' is not a defined term; the test suite author / TTCN-3 module writer is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- The user, however, shall ensure that all type recursion is resolvable and that no infinite recursion occurs.

requirements.original: The user, however, shall ensure that all type recursion is resolvable and that no infinite recursion occurs.
requirements.canonical: A recursive type definition SHALL NOT cause infinite recursion.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- The user, however, shall ensure that all type recursion is resolvable and that no infinite recursion occurs.

requirements.original: In case of record and set types, to avoid infinite recursion, fields referencing to its own type, shall be optional.
requirements.canonical: In a record or set type, a field referencing its own enclosing type SHALL be optional.

ambiguity.issue: 'referencing its own type' can mean a field whose type is directly the enclosing type, or any field whose type (indirectly) contains the enclosing type, e.g. via a union; the direct reading was chosen.
readings: In a record or set type, a field whose type is the enclosing record or set type SHALL be optional.
In a record or set type, every field whose type directly or indirectly references the enclosing type SHALL be optional.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- In case of record and set types, to avoid infinite recursion, fields referencing to its own type, shall be optional.

requirements.original: In case of union types, to avoid infinite recursion, at least one of the alternatives shall not reference its own type.
requirements.canonical: In a union type, at least one alternative SHALL NOT reference the union type itself.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.0 -- In case of union types, to avoid infinite recursion, at least one of the alternatives shall not reference its own type.

requirements.original: The fields of a record type may be of any TTCN-3 type.
requirements.canonical: A field of a record type MAY be of any TTCN-3 type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- The fields of a record type may be of any TTCN-3 type.

requirements.original: The values of a record shall be compatible with the types of the record fields.
requirements.canonical: Each field value of a record value SHALL be compatible with the type of the corresponding record field.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- The values of a record shall be compatible with the types of the record fields.

requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).
requirements.canonical: A field identifier of a record type IS local to that record type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).
requirements.canonical: A field identifier SHALL be unique within its record type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).
requirements.canonical: A field identifier of a record type NEED NOT be globally unique.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.original: Records may be defined with no fields, i.e. as empty records.
requirements.canonical: A record type MAY be defined with no fields (empty record).

examples.text: type record MyEmptyRecord {}

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- Records may be defined with no fields, i.e. as empty records.

requirements.original: The order of field values in the value list notation shall be the same as the order of fields in the related type definition.
requirements.canonical: In value list notation for a record value, the order of the field values SHALL be the same as the order of the fields in the record type definition.

examples.text: v_myRecordValue:= {v_myIntegerValue, {'11001'B, true}, "A string"};

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- The order of field values in the value list notation shall be the same as the order of fields in the related type definition.

requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used for record-s, fields wished to be changed shall be identified explicitly and a value, the not used symbol "-" or the omit keyword can be associated with them.
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used for a record value, each field to be changed SHALL be identified explicitly.
requirements.condition: the assignment notation is used for a record value
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- When the assignment notation is used for record-s, fields wished to be changed shall be identified explicitly and a value, the not used symbol "-" or the omit keyword can be associated with them.

requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used for record-s, fields wished to be changed shall be identified explicitly and a value, the not used symbol "-" or the omit keyword can be associated with them.
requirements.canonical: In assignment notation for a record value, an explicitly identified field MAY be associated with a value, the not used symbol "-" or the `omit` keyword.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- When the assignment notation is used for record-s, fields wished to be changed shall be identified explicitly and a value, the not used symbol "-" or the omit keyword can be associated with them.

requirements.original: The `omit` keyword shall only be used for optional fields.
requirements.canonical: In assignment notation, the `omit` keyword SHALL only be used for optional fields.
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used for a record value
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- The `omit` keyword shall only be used for optional fields.

requirements.original: Its result is that the given field is not present in the given value.
requirements.canonical: An optional field assigned `omit` in assignment notation IS not present in the resulting value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- Its result is that the given field is not present in the given value.

requirements.original: Mandatory fields, not explicitly referred to in the notation or explicitly unspecified using the not used symbol "-", shall remain unchanged.
requirements.canonical: A mandatory field that is not explicitly referred to in the assignment notation, or is explicitly unspecified using the not used symbol "-", SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- Mandatory fields, not explicitly referred to in the notation or explicitly unspecified using the not used symbol "-", shall remain unchanged.

requirements.original: In particular, when specifying partial values (i.e. setting the value of only a subset of the fields) using the assignment notation, at initialization, only the fields to be assigned values shall be specified.
requirements.canonical: When a partial value is specified using the assignment notation at initialization, only the fields to be assigned values SHALL be specified.
requirements.condition: partial value specified with assignment notation at initialization

ambiguity.issue: 'only ... shall be specified' can be read as a relaxation (other fields need not be listed) or as a prohibition of listing other fields; the relaxation reading was chosen as it matches the surrounding text and examples.
readings: When a partial value is specified using the assignment notation at initialization, only the fields to be assigned values NEED be specified.
When a partial value is specified using the assignment notation at initialization, fields not assigned a value SHALL NOT be listed (e.g. with the not used symbol).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- In particular, when specifying partial values (i.e. setting the value of only a subset of the fields) using the assignment notation, at initialization, only the fields to be assigned values shall be specified.

requirements.original: Fields not mentioned are implicitly left uninitialized.
requirements.canonical: At initialization with the assignment notation, a field not mentioned in the notation IS implicitly left uninitialized.
requirements.condition: the optional attribute is not "implicit omit"
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- Fields not mentioned are implicitly left uninitialized.

requirements.original: When re-assigning a previously initialized value, using the not used symbol or just skipping a field in an assignment notation, will cause that field to remain unchanged.
requirements.canonical: When a previously initialized value is re-assigned using the assignment notation, a field skipped or given the not used symbol "-" IS left unchanged.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- When re-assigning a previously initialized value, using the not used symbol or just skipping a field in an assignment notation, will cause that field to remain unchanged.

requirements.original: Even when specifying partial values each field shall not appear more than once.
requirements.canonical: A field SHALL NOT appear more than once in an assignment notation, also when a partial value is specified.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- Even when specifying partial values each field shall not appear more than once.

requirements.original: Omitted optional fields are not present in the record or set value intentionally, i.e. the field is initialized and it does not prevent the whole record or set from being completely initialized.
requirements.canonical: An omitted optional field IS NOT an obstacle to the record or set value being completely initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- Omitted optional fields are not present in the record or set value intentionally, i.e. the field is initialized and it does not prevent the whole record or set from being completely initialized.

requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", optional and mandatory fields, not directly referred to in the notation shall remain unchanged.
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", optional and mandatory fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", optional and mandatory fields, not directly referred to in the notation shall remain unchanged.

requirements.original: When optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly, they are uninitialized (i.e. the optional attribute shall not have any effect on variables as described in clause 27.7 restriction a)).
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a variable that is not assigned explicitly IS uninitialized.
requirements.condition: optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- When optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly, they are uninitialized (i.e. the optional attribute shall not have any effect on variables as described in clause 27.7 restriction a)).

requirements.original: When optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly, they are uninitialized (i.e. the optional attribute shall not have any effect on variables as described in clause 27.7 restriction a)).
requirements.canonical: The optional attribute SHALL NOT have any effect on variables.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- When optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly, they are uninitialized (i.e. the optional attribute shall not have any effect on variables as described in clause 27.7 restriction a)).

requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is set to "implicit `omit",` optional fields, not directly referred to in the notation, shall implicitly be set to omit, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", optional fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL implicitly be set to `omit`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is set to "implicit `omit",` optional fields, not directly referred to in the notation, shall implicitly be set to omit, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is set to "implicit `omit",` optional fields, not directly referred to in the notation, shall implicitly be set to omit, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", mandatory fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.1.0 -- When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is set to "implicit `omit",` optional fields, not directly referred to in the notation, shall implicitly be set to omit, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).
